newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO work together to recover soldier's body.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO work together to recover soldier's body.

text.p: Israel and the PLO said on Friday they worked together despite a breakdown in security coordination to find the body of an Israeli soldier kidnapped by an Islamist group seven months ago.

But in a further sign of tensions, Israeli troops shot and wounded 16 Arabs while battling hundreds of stone-throwers on a fourth straight day of clashes in the West Bank town of Hebron, south of Jerusalem, hospital officials said.

Israeli security forces found the body of Sergeant Sharon Edri, 19, in Sourif village in the West Bank on Thursday after Israeli and Palestinian security forces each arrested two members of a six-man Hamas squad suspected of killing him.

Palestinian forces detained a fifth suspect on Friday in the PLO-controlled West Bank town of Bethlehem. The Israeli army sealed off the homes of three suspects in Sourif and informed owners it planned to demolish them later.
The sealing sparked clashes in the village where Israeli soldiers shot a 12-year-old Palestinian girl with a rubber bullet, wounding her in the leg, witnesses said.
The sixth member of the Hamas squad died last month when an explosive charge he meant to leave at a Tel Aviv cafe exploded prematurely, killing him and three Israeli women.

Security coordination between Israel and the PLO broke down in March after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, ignoring world pleas, sent bulldozers to work on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Netanyahu, who had accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of giving a "green light" to Islamic militants to attack Israelis, said PLO security forces had helped crack the case of the missing soldier.

"In the last part of the operation...the Palestinian Authority arrested two members of the squad and through their arrest we were able to determine finally the place where Edri was buried," he said during a visit to the Netherlands.

Arafat's aide Marwan Kanafani confirmed in an interview with Reuters that the Palestinian Authority helped to locate Edri's body. But he insisted humanitarian rather than political considerations guided it.
"This is an issue of humanitarian reasons not of security coordination with the Israelis," Kanafani said. "It has nothing to do with any political reasons."
Washington has sought to restore security coordination between the two sides. But Palestinian security officials demand the Jewish state first stop all settlement building.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai discussed Israeli-Palestinian relations with U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk in Tel Aviv on Friday, a defence ministry spokesman said.

Israel Channel Two television and Army radio reported on Friday that U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross will return to Israel next week to try to break the impasse in negotiations. They did not give a date for his return.
Israeli security sources said Arafat gave orders to arrest the Hamas suspects after he met U.S. CIA and Israeli security officials in Gaza on Tuesday.

"When the appeal was made to Arafat in this instance, they responded immediately with a meeting and also the instructions to his people to do what they can in this instance in order to help," Israeli army chief Amnon Shahak told army radio.
"There were very clear instructions and so too were they carried out," he said.

A senior Palestinian police officer in Gaza said that Israeli authorities had informed the Palestinian side on Friday that crossing points between Gaza and Israel would be reopened for labourers and trade as of Sunday.
The Israeli army sealed off its borders with Gaza and the West Bank after the cafe bombing, cutting off thousands of Palestinian labourers from jobs in the Jewish state.
"We were told the situation will be restored to what it was before this closure,"said Major-General Abdel-Razek al-Majaydeh, director-general of Gaza's Palestinian National Security Forces.
